newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes flat in becalmed holiday market.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes flat in becalmed holiday market.

text.p: North Sea spot crudes were notionally unchanged on Monday with many players absent due to a national holiday in Britain, traders said.
"This is a day when those in their offices will be doing anything but trading," said a trader at a Norwegian producer.

Paper June Brent was assessed unchanged at around $17.95-$18 a barrel in line with Friday's close on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) which was shut on Monday, but the prompt intermonth spread eased back.
June/July was pegged at -17/-13 cents, two or three cents weaker after deals at -15 cents in late U.S. activity on Friday.
No Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Monday.
There was slightly more activity in the Mediterranean, where a very prompt Urals cargo was offered at a slightly softer Dated Brent -$1.00 a barrel cif Augusta.
Libya told customers it was leaving the May price of its key Es Sider crude unchanged at Dated Brent -40 cents a barrel.
Saudi Arabia, however, lifted its June price of Arab Light by 10 cents a barrel to Dated Brent less $2.05 for European customers, pushing Iraqi Kirkuk Blend up to Dated Brent less $2.00.
Despite the increase, traders said Kirkuk should maintain its competitive edge against rival Russian Urals.
"With Urals still around (dated) Brent minus $1.00 then Kirkuk still looks very good at (dated)minus $2.00," said a term customer.
